script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Weight of Silence

FADE IN:

INT. APARTMENT - NIGHT

The room is dimly lit by the glow of a computer screen. JAMES, a young man in his late twenties, hunches over a keyboard, typing with furious intensity.

JAMES
(Whispering to himself)
Come on... almost there.

The door creaks open, and in walks SARAH, a girl James met online. She stands in the doorway, a faint smile on her face.

SARAH
Is everything okay? You've been up all night.

James jumps, startled, and closes his laptop with a snap.

JAMES
(Nervously)
Just a little project.

Sarah steps closer, her curiosity piqued. She notices the cluttered state of the apartment, the piles of takeout containers and empty water bottles.

SARAH
(Gently)
You really should get some rest.

James sighs, rubbing his eyes.

JAMES
I'll be fine.

Sarah looks at him, concern etched on her features. She takes a seat next to him on the couch.

SARAH
If you say so. But I'm here if you need to talk.

They sit in silence for a moment, the only sound being the ticking of the clock.

FADE OUT.

INT. CAFETERIA - DAY

James and Sarah sit at a table, surrounded by the chatter of other students. They exchange friendly banter as they eat their lunches.

SARAH
So, what's this project you were working on last night?

James hesitates, then shrugs.

JAMES
Just something for a class.

Sarah raises an eyebrow, but doesn't press the issue. Instead, she shares a story about her own experiences with difficult projects.

FADE OUT.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James lies in bed, staring at the ceiling. The room is dark except for the faint glow of the alarm clock. He hears a soft knock on the door.

JAMES
(Calling out)
Come in.

Sarah enters, carrying a steaming mug of tea. She sits down next to James and hands him the mug.

SARAH
(Gently)
You look like you've seen a ghost.

James takes a sip of the tea, the warmth spreading through his body.

JAMES
(Sighing)
It's just been a tough week.

Sarah nods sympathetically. They sit in silence for a moment, the only sound being the ticking of the clock.

SARAH
(Softly)
Do you want to talk about it?

James hesitates, then finally opens up about the stresses in his life - the demanding class schedule, the pressure to succeed, the weight of his own expectations. Sarah listens intently, offering words of support and encouragement.

FADE OUT.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

James and Sarah sit at a table, surrounded by stacks of books. They've come to the library to study together, and James seems more focused than he has in weeks.

SARAH
(Smiling)
You're really getting into the flow of things now.

James looks up, a small smile playing at the corners of his lips.

JAMES
Thanks, Sarah. Your support means a lot to me.

They continue their study session, the only sounds being the turning of pages and the occasional hushed whisper.

FADE OUT.

INT. APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits at his computer, his face lit by the screen. Sarah enters the room, carrying a tray of takeout food.

SARAH
I thought we could use a break.

James looks up, a grateful expression on his face.

JAMES
You always know how to make things better.

They eat together in silence, the only sounds being the clinking of utensils and the occasional bite of food.

FADE OUT.

INT. CLASSROOM - DAY

James sits in the front row of the classroom, a stack of papers in front of him. He looks up as the professor enters, followed by Sarah. She takes a seat next to him, a small smile on her face.

The professor begins to distribute the graded papers, and James' heart races as he takes his. He looks at Sarah, who gives him a reassuring nod. He opens the paper, his heart sinking as he reads the failing grade.

SARAH
(Whispering)
It's just one class. You'll get through it.

James nods, taking a deep breath. He looks up at Sarah, a gratitude shining in his eyes.

FADE OUT.

INT. APARTMENT - NIGHT

James and Sarah sit on the couch, surrounded by a pile of textbooks and notes. James looks at Sarah, his expression serious.

JAMES
I don't know what I'd do without you.

Sarah smiles, reaching out to take his hand.

SARAH
You'll get through this, James. And I'll be here for you every step of the way.

They sit in silence, the only sound being the ticking of the clock.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
